trap-nonspeakable.notes: MATH FINDING to report (not edited): the closing claim 'the adjoint trace recovers the Killing form on su(2): tr_Ad(f) = tr(ad(f)) = -2 tr_{C^2}(f)' does not say what it means to say. Computed symbolically (sympy, gl(2) basis): tr(ad X) = 0 for every X in su(2) - ad is traceless on any perfect Lie algebra - and tr_{C^2}(X) = 0 too, so the displayed chain is 0 = 0 = 0, vacuously true on su(2) and false off it (f = id gives tr(ad f) = 0 but -2 tr(f) = -4). The Killing form is moreover a BILINEAR form, not a linear functional: B(X,Y) = tr(ad X ad Y), and on su(2) the computed ratio B(X,X)/tr(X^2) is exactly 4 (tr(ad^2) = -8 against tr(X^2) = -2 on each of the three standard generators), so the normalisation is +4 tr(XY), not -2 tr(X). The sentence above it is fine; what should presumably be claimed is that the induced pairing <f,g>_Ad, not the trace of a single endomorphism, recovers the Killing form, with coefficient 4.
